title: verify: SignedData signer_infos count not bounded — potential DoS
description:
In verify.rs, all SignerInfo entries in the SignedData are processed in a collect() without any limit:

  let signers: Vec<SignerResult> = sd.signer_infos.0.iter()
      .map(|si| verify_one(...))
      .collect();

Each verify_one() call performs: a SHA-2 digest over signed_content, a DER encode of signed_attrs, a cert lookup over the bag, and an RSA or ECDSA signature verification. RSA verification in particular is CPU-intensive.

A crafted SignedData with 1,000 SignerInfo entries forces 1,000 full RSA verifications on the caller's thread.

What goes wrong: a server calling verify() on untrusted input can be driven to 100% CPU for seconds per message, enabling DoS.

Affected code: verify.rs lines 117-131.

Fix: cap the number of SignerInfo entries processed (e.g. reject if signer_infos.len() > 10 or a caller-configurable limit). Return MalformedInput if the cap is exceeded.
